dropped.8: `agent({ tools })` is gone: a tool is declared by its FILE. `tools/incident_create.ts` that default-exports `tool({ … })` IS the tool `incident_create`, enumerated where the bundle is assembled and named by nothing — so the map every epoch up to 8 was authored with no longer type-checks, and `tools` on the parameter shape is now the InlineToolsMisuse message naming the file to create. The map restated a rule the filesystem already carried, and the cost was not its 62 lines: forgetting one was SILENT, so the file compiled, every gate passed, and the tool never reached the model. A resolved registry goes on with `withTools`, which is what the build and `withDiscoveredTools` both call.
dropped.9: AgentDef lost its state type parameter, its `state` factory and `InferAgentState`: session state belongs to a sessionSlot, which types and stores its own value, so there is no per-agent state shape to thread. `syncState` takes that slot's projection rather than a function over the whole bag.
dropped.14: The ten field-list and message types behind AgentParams' four arms (DefaultedAgentField, FrontDoorField, InlineToolsField, InlineToolsMisuse, PipelineOnlyField, PipelineOnlyMisuse, ProviderField, StaticFrontDoorMisuse, WorkflowAppMisuse, WorkflowAppOnlyField) left the root barrel. They are the IMPLEMENTATION of a compile error — an author reads them in the message tsc prints, never by name — and the root's own membership test is whether an agent.ts would name a symbol. They still type the arms, so every error message is unchanged; what is gone is ten entries in an authoring autocomplete. Epoch 14's example named PipelineOnlyMisuse directly, which nothing outside this repo had reason to do.

dropped.1: Epoch 1's shape — `const rates: Rates = await fetchJson<Rates>(url)` — no longer compiles, deliberately. The three network builtins ANSWER with `{ error }` rather than throwing (a model-facing contract that is not changing), and typing them `Promise<T>` made that invisible: all three callers in this repo wrote `?? []` / `?? ""` and turned a live DuckDuckGo 403 into "the web has nothing". The return type is `T | ToolFailure` now, so a caller that names a shape must narrow with `isToolFailure`. An UNTYPED call is unaffected — `DefaultToolResult` is `any` — so only the call sites precise enough to have a shape are asked to handle the failure they were already receiving.

Three constants left the root barrel for @alexkroman1/aai/internal: MAX_PLAYBACK_BUFFERED_MS and PLAYBACK_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS are client-audio budgets and DEFAULT_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS is a runtime deadline, none of which an agent() field sets. This capability is the published answer to 'what happens if I leave this field off', and those three answer no field.

flow() is dialog(): Flow -> Dialog, FlowPosition -> DialogPosition, FlowToolDef -> DialogToolDef, FlowToolResult -> DialogToolResult, FlowOptions -> DialogOptions. A pure rename, and the argument is the import line: 'flow' sat in the same barrel as 'workflow' meaning something entirely different (a dialog statechart bound to a session, versus durable work that outlives it), and next to graph(), whose name said equally little about which of the two you wanted. dialog() / procedure() / workflow() is a legible triple — where the conversation is, one unit of work inside a tool call, and work that survives the session.

graph() is procedure(): Graph -> Procedure, GraphRunOptions -> ProcedureRunOptions, GraphNotFinishedError -> ProcedureNotFinishedError, and the error's `graph` field is `procedure`. Same rename, same argument as aai:dialog — 'graph' described the implementation (an XState machine) rather than the job (a unit of work you invoke and that returns), and gave a reader no way to tell it from flow().

Not a change to this capability's own surface — `sessionSlot` and every method on it are untouched, and epochs 3 through 7 still compile. Its `updateTool` body is `async`, and a mutation window is synchronous now — the draft is stored when the body returns, so an await inside one writes to a value that has already been stored. The SDK refuses it at run time naming the rule, and `pnpm typecheck` (this mechanism's whole gate) cannot see that. Recording it as dropped rather than leaving a green example that throws on its first call is the honest reading of what "supported" claims.

dropped.11: The step surface left /utils for @alexkroman1/aai/step, and the platform contracts and wire helpers left it for /internal. That subpath's membership rule was a BUILD property — 'zod-free, so the CLI can import it on every invocation' — which is true, load-bearing, and not something anybody imports BY: nobody reaches for a module because of its dependency graph. Seventy-nine exports served three unrelated readers (a step body, a tool body, and the framework's own plumbing), so the import line said nothing about which layer you were in. It is fifteen now, all of them written inside a tool body. The zod-free budget is unchanged and now holds on /internal too.
